accounting_scope: Eq factors require 2^floor(d/2)+2^ceil(d/2) Fp3 elements per lookup, plus Poly/allocator metadata; lookup tables captured by a getter live with that getter. Local tables and power iterator states are owned proof memory beyond State::named_bytes. The retained-generation getter keeps its existing dynamic-prefix handling; this is not full PCS source-uniformity or a new Lean claim. The retained S1 vector is additional live proof storage, not a dense original A or full RS codeword, and its allocation capacity remains reserved through truncations until state drop. The <=16-variable residual guard remains unchanged. Each live installed W or accepted/pending A owns its retained tree and initial pads for the lifetime of that source. These persist alongside the other live roots and all proof workspaces; folded generation leases remain separate. Reduced Merkle openings share regenerated rows across subtrees in the same public batch; no change to algebra, source/pad offsets, MAC reservations, transcript or original PCS endpoint. The caller owns each base-field row batch alongside sorted queries, opened row copies, all required subtree digests/salts and the retained top cache. open_subtree_bytes_each accounts only for one subtree digest/salt payload, not full opening memory. Every evaluation-tree node retains modulus and reciprocal spectra. Coefficient levels and Newton intermediates during setup, parent/child remainder levels during descent, points, DFT workspace and output remain owned memory. Not canonical 2^21 query admission, a single scan of the whole opening, a GPU pipeline, complete work/peak ledger or real Gamma. No time or arena margin credit.

ReplayModel retains the original top Merkle cache, salt offsets/RNG snapshot and pads at construction. Initial handles share that immutable tree without source reads or recommitment; proof coins and MACs remain fresh. The retained-handle test covers cache ownership, no source reads on handle creation, reproducible openings and changed-source rejection. The full WHIR wire oracle now uses that same initial cache and compares the original pads. An independent direct-product/truncated-inverse oracle covers powers of two through 1024, repeated and zero points. The source callback keeps its existing 1024-request cap, points/order, source reads, private pads and block reduction. Required subtrees are grouped into batches of at most 1024 distinct rows; the same rows feed subtree hashes and the requested openings, with no separate query callback.
